relevance_note: Case series of three children with arterial tortuosity syndrome and homozygous SLC2A10 variants: "We describe 3 children with genetically confirmed ATS".
method_note: Hand extraction from a short case series; JSON assembled with a small Python script in the scratch directory, every value from my reading. Table 1 has patients as columns (headers 'Case 1', 'Case 2', 'Case 3'). Labels are the paper's own 'Case 1/2/3'. No SLC2A10 variant description is printed for any patient (only 'homozygous pathogenic variant in SLC2A10'), so variant_original_string is 'not reported' for all three rows. Case 1 is identified as 'the neonatal patient'/'a neonate' in the abstract and comparative summary, Case 2 as 'the older infant'/'15-month-old infant'. The two cousins with congenital heart disease (Case 1 family history) were given no rows: they are not described as having ATS or an SLC2A10 variant, nor tested. Age at presentation (Table 1) was not entered as age at last evaluation for Case 1, because his course continued after referral at 3 weeks; for Cases 2 and 3 the stated age at the evaluation described was used. Group statements: the abstract sentence 'Imaging in these cases revealed ... without aneurysm formation, dissection, or significant obstruction' was used (inferred from group statement) to exclude aneurysm/dissection where the case text is silent; 'significant obstruction' was not used to exclude the stenosis checklist items (narrower absence). Case 1 has 'mild dilation of the ascending aorta' but the paper states no aneurysm; aortic root aneurysm checklist recorded excluded on that explicit statement. Possible contradiction for Case 2: echocardiography reports 'normal ventricular size and function' whereas the Fig. 3 legend reports 'Global cardiomegaly with marked enlargement of the left side of the heart'; both rows emitted (no checklist item affected). Also echo-normal ventricular size alongside referral for known left ventricular hypertrophy (hypertrophy recorded observed from referral and Table 1). Case 3 'bulging sternum (pectus deformity)' was recorded as observed for the checklist item 'pectus excavatum or carinatum' (a bulging sternum is a protrusion); the paper does not name the type. Case 2 pulmonary artery flow turbulence (gradient 14 mmHg) is not called stenosis by the authors, so pulmonary artery stenosis is not reported. Referral reasons 'bronchiolitis' and 'suspected congenital heart disease' for Case 1 were not recorded as features (evaluation reasons, not findings).
